construct: During sensitization, IgE binds high-affinity Fc epsilon RI receptors on mast cells. On re-exposure, multivalent allergen cross-links receptor-bound IgE, triggering mast-cell activation and rapid mediator release.

notes: Immunoglobulin E — StatPearls: IgE binds Fc epsilon RI on mast cells/basophils; allergen binding triggers mediator release.
Physiology, Immune Response — StatPearls 2026: type I hypersensitivity involves cross-linking surface-bound IgE and mast-cell mediator release.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: In a sensitized patient, mast cells bear allergen-specific IgE on Fc epsilon RI. Re-exposure cross-links adjacent complexes, activating mast cells and causing rapid histamine/lipid mediator release.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: IgE can bind both mast cells and basophils, but the stem explicitly asks for the mast-cell trigger. Cross-linking Fc epsilon RI-bound IgE is the defining immediate type I event; the other choices map to different immune mechanisms.
